title: How to Wear a Paperclip Chain Necklace (Without Overthinking It)
excerpt: A paperclip chain looks best worn high and visible over an open neckline. Here's how to style, layer and size one — plus what 48cm looks like on.

content.text: Wear a paperclip chain where people can see the links — over an open collar, a crew neck, a bare chest, never buried under a scarf. The flat, elongated links are the whole point, so give them space. A 48cm chain sits just below the collarbone on most people, which is the easiest length to wear alone or as the middle piece in a layered stack.
That's the short answer. Below, the details that decide whether it looks sharp or muddled: length, necklines, layering order, and where a front clasp changes the whole thing.
Where does a 48cm paperclip chain actually sit?

On most adults, 48cm lands right at or just under the collarbone — sometimes called princess length. It's the most forgiving length there is. It clears a high neckline instead of fighting it, it doesn't disappear into a V-neck, and it sits above the bust so it doesn't move around when you do.

To check it on yourself before you buy anything: take a piece of string, lay it around your neck, mark where 48cm closes, and look in the mirror. If you have a larger neck or a broader chest, that same chain will sit slightly higher — still fine, just closer to a collar-hugging look than a drop. If you want it lower, layer it with something longer rather than trying to make one chain do two jobs.

Our Paperclip Chain Diamond Initial Necklace is 48cm with a front toggle clasp, and the rhinestone initial hangs straight off that clasp. So the decorative part sits front and centre by design — you're not chasing a pendant that keeps sliding to the back of your neck.
What necklines does a paperclip chain look best with?
Chunky links need contrast. Put them against flat, simple fabric and they read as deliberate. Put them against busy prints, ruffles or a wide statement collar and everything competes.
Necklines that work, from easiest to most interesting:
items: Crew neck tee or fine-knit jumper — the chain lies on the fabric, fully visible, no styling needed.
Open shirt with the top two buttons undone — the chain sits in the gap, the toggle bar catches the light where the placket ends.
Scoop or boat neck — plenty of skin, and 48cm stops well above the neckline edge so nothing tangles.
Turtleneck — this is where chunky links earn their place. Wear it over, not under, and let the chain be the only thing happening up top.
Blazer over a plain tee — the chain fills the V made by the lapels. One of the best autumn combinations, and it survives a coat going on and off.
Strappy top or a bare shoulder — a wider link balances out exposed collarbones better than a thin chain does.

content.text: The one to avoid: a wide cowl or a chunky cable-knit collar that swallows the chain. If the fabric is thicker than the links, the chain loses.
How do you layer a paperclip chain with other necklaces?

Two rules, and then you're free. First, the paperclip stays the widest link in the stack — everything else you add should be visibly thinner so the eye knows where to land. Second, leave 4–6cm between each chain so they don't rub together and sit as one tangled band.
A stack that works, built from the top down:
items: Short piece, around 38–40cm: a choker or a beaded chain that sits at the base of the neck. A Turquoise Beaded Cable Chain Necklace adds colour and a different texture without adding bulk.
Middle piece, 48cm: the paperclip chain with the initial. This is your anchor — the widest link, the most visible detail.
Long piece, 55cm or more: a fine chain with a small charm that drops below the others. A Birth Flower Charm Necklace works here if you want the stack to carry some meaning as well as shape.

content.text: Two chains is enough for most days. Three is for when the rest of the outfit is plain. If you're wearing all three and it feels like too much, take out the middle one — but then you've removed the best bit, so it's usually the short one that goes.

Keep the metal tone consistent within a stack unless you're deliberately mixing. Gold-tone paperclip with gold-tone chains reads clean. Add silver and you need to commit to it across at least two pieces so it looks chosen, not accidental.
Is a paperclip chain necklace unisex?

Yes, and it's one of the few chain styles that genuinely is. The links are geometric rather than decorative — no scallops, no filigree, nothing gendered about a rectangle. That's why you see paperclip chains on everyone.

For a more masculine look, wear it alone at 48cm over a plain tee or an open shirt, no layering. For a softer look, layer it and let the initial charm sit against skin rather than fabric. Same necklace, two completely different reads.

The front toggle clasp helps here too. A toggle is a design feature, not something you hide at the back — the bar slots through the ring and sits flat at the front of your neckline. It's also the easiest closure to do one-handed, which matters more than you'd think on a cold morning.
Does a gold paperclip initial necklace work as a gift?

It's one of the safer personalised gifts, because you're not guessing taste — you're guessing a letter, and you already know the letter. A paperclip chain is a shape that's been in constant wear for years now, so it's not going to date the way a trend charm might.
How to choose the letter:
items: Their first initial — the default, and the one most people want.
The initial of a partner, child or someone they've lost — quieter, and more meaningful if you know the story.
Their surname initial — good for someone who goes by a nickname and doesn't feel attached to their given first name.
A shared initial between two people, if you're buying matching pieces for a pair.

content.text: At €30 it sits in the range where a gift feels considered without being heavy. If you're buying for someone in Europe and shipping matters, ours dispatches within 1–2 business days. Worth noting for December — the gap between "I'll order next week" and "it's too late" closes fast once mid-month hits.
Will it survive being worn every day?

That depends entirely on what it's made of. A plated brass paperclip chain will wear through at the link joints where the metal rubs against itself — chunky chains move a lot, and that's exactly where colour goes first. Stainless steel with a PVD finish holds up far better, because the coating is bonded rather than sitting on the surface.

Ours is stainless steel with an 18K PVD real gold plated finish, waterproof, tarnish-resistant and hypoallergenic. You can wear it in the shower, at the sea, in the rain on the way to work. What it still wants: a wipe with a soft cloth after each wear, and storage in an airtight container when you're not wearing it. Perfume and hairspray go on first, necklace goes on last.

If you're building a small stack of everyday necklaces rather than buying one piece, this is the one to make chunky. Fine chains are easy to find and easy to replace. A good paperclip chain that keeps its colour is the piece you'll reach for most, and it's worth getting right.
Each of ours is made by hand by the two of us here in Portugal, so no two are identical and slight variations happen. That's the nature of it.

faq.question: What's the difference between a paperclip chain and a cable chain?
faq.answer: A paperclip chain has long, flat, elongated oval links — the shape of an actual paperclip — and usually reads as chunkier and more graphic. A cable chain has short, round or oval links of even proportion and sits flatter and finer against the skin. Paperclip chains hold their shape better when worn alone; cable chains disappear more easily into a layered stack.

faq.question: Does a paperclip chain necklace with a toggle clasp go over your head?
faq.answer: No, and it isn't meant to. A toggle clasp opens completely — you slide the bar out of the ring, put the chain around your neck and slot it back in at the front. It's easier to fasten one-handed than a lobster clasp and the clasp itself stays visible as part of the design.

faq.question: Can you wear a paperclip chain necklace to work?
faq.answer: Yes. At 48cm it sits just below the collarbone, above most shirt and blouse necklines, so it reads as one clean piece rather than a statement. Worn alone over a plain top or in the V of a blazer it stays office-appropriate; save the three-chain stack for after hours.

title: October Birth Flower: Marigold & Cosmos Meaning
excerpt: October has two birth flowers: marigold and cosmos. Marigold means warmth, devotion and grief remembered. Cosmos means order, peace and harmony in love.

content.text: October has two birth flowers: the marigold and the cosmos. The marigold stands for warmth, devotion, and love that holds on through grief — it's the flower of remembrance, the one laid out for Día de los Muertos and burned in lamps at Diwali. The cosmos means order, balance and peace, a flower named after the Greek word for a harmonious universe, and it's usually read as a wish for calm and tranquil love.

So if you're born in October, you get both a fiery flower and a gentle one. That's a useful thing when you're choosing jewelry or a gift, because the two meanings pull in different directions and you can pick the one that fits the person.
What does the marigold birth flower mean?

Marigold meaning comes down to three things that sit together: devotion, warmth, and remembering someone who's gone. The colour does a lot of the work here — deep orange and gold, the same shades as October light in Europe, when the sun sits low and everything goes amber around five in the afternoon.

In Mexico, marigolds (cempasúchil) are the flowers that guide the dead home on 1 and 2 November. The petals get scattered in paths from the door to the altar. In India, marigold garlands hang over doorways at Diwali and get strung for weddings, where they mean auspicious beginnings and a blessing on the household. In older European flower language, marigold carried a heavier note — grief, and sometimes jealousy or the pain of loving someone you can't have. That sounds grim, but it's really about intensity. Marigold is not a polite flower. It's the one that says I feel this strongly.

Practically, what this means for a gift: marigold suits someone with a lot of heart. A mother. A friend who shows up. Someone who lost somebody this year and would like a piece that quietly holds that. Gold-tone metal is the obvious match — it reads as marigold without needing the flower spelled out.
What does the cosmos flower symbolise?

Cosmos is the calmer half of October. The name comes from the Greek kosmos, meaning order and harmony — the botanist who named it was struck by how evenly spaced the petals are. Eight petals, laid out like a wheel. So the symbolism is balance, wholeness, and a love that's peaceful rather than dramatic.

Cosmos also carries modesty and tranquility. It's a flower that keeps blooming late into autumn, right through October, long after most summer flowers have given up. That's part of why it landed as an October birth flower in the first place. There's something in that for a gift message: still going, still gentle, still here.
Colour changes the reading slightly, if you want to be precise about it:
Cosmos colours and what they're usually taken to mean:
items: White cosmos — purity, a fresh start, and the easiest one to translate into jewelry (think pearl and silver-tone)
Pink cosmos — soft affection, the flower you'd give a close friend rather than a partner
Deep magenta and burgundy cosmos — romantic love with a bit more weight to it, good for an anniversary that lands in October
Chocolate cosmos — rare and a bit strange-looking, associated with secrets and things unsaid; a cult favourite among flower people

content.text: How do you wear the October birth flower as jewelry?
You don't need a literal flower charm. Most of the time the nicer move is to translate the flower into colour and material, so the piece works every day instead of only on a birthday.

For marigold, go gold-tone and warm. Anything in that amber-to-brass range does the job, and it sits well against the knitwear everyone's already pulling out at the end of September. A Gold Beaded Cross Bracelet (€30) gives you that marigold warmth with texture rather than a pictorial flower — the small beads catch light the way petals do. Stack it with a watch, or wear two on the same wrist.

For cosmos, go pearl and pale. Freshwater pearl reads as white cosmos almost exactly — round, soft, no shine that shouts. A Layered Pearl Bracelet (€24) gives you the layered, overlapping look of cosmos petals in one piece. If you want the pink cosmos reading, a Pink Cross Charm Bracelet (€24) is the closest colour match in the range, and it's small enough to wear with anything.

If the person in question is an October baby, you can also stack the birth flower idea with their sign. October covers Libra (until 22 or 23 October) and Scorpio (from 23 October). A Zodiac Charm Bracelet (€24) next to a pearl one gives you flower-plus-sign on the same wrist without anything looking matchy. Libra and cosmos actually line up neatly — both are about balance. Scorpio and marigold line up too, both being about intensity and things that survive.
What's a good October birthday gift under €30?

Most October birthdays are in the next four weeks, so here's the practical version, sorted by what you're spending. Everything here is stainless steel — waterproof, tarnish-resistant, fine in the shower and in the sea, which matters if you're giving it to someone who never takes jewelry off.
By budget:
items: Around €24 — one bracelet, wrapped on its own. The Pink Cross Charm Bracelet for the cosmos reading, or the Zodiac Charm Bracelet for a Libra or Scorpio. Write the flower meaning on the card; that's what turns it into a birth flower gift.

€28 — something with their initial on it. The Pearl Heart Initial Bracelet pairs pearl (white cosmos) with a letter, so it's personal without being fussy. This is the safest gift on the list if you don't know their taste well.
€30 and up — go gold-tone for the marigold half of October. The Gold Beaded Cross Bracelet works alone, and it's the one that holds up under a coat sleeve all winter.
€50-ish — two bracelets, one pearl and one gold-tone, given as a pair. That's both October flowers in one box, and it's the version people remember.

content.text: On sizing: measure the wrist with a strip of paper and a ruler, then add about 1.5 cm for a comfortable fit. Most women's wrists land between 14 and 17 cm, so a 16–17 cm bracelet suits the majority. If you're guessing, guess slightly long — a bracelet that slides is wearable, one that pinches isn't.
Marigold or cosmos — which one should you pick?
Pick based on the person, not the month. Here's the short version we use when someone asks us at the studio.
Choose marigold if:
items: The gift is for a mother, grandmother, or someone who mothers everybody
It's a remembrance piece, or the first birthday after a loss
The person wears warm metals, tan, rust, olive, brown
You want the gift to feel bold rather than delicate
Their birthday falls in late October, near Día de los Muertos and Diwali, and the timing feels right

content.text: Choose cosmos if the person is calmer in how they dress, wears a lot of white and cream, likes small things, or is going through something and could use a piece that means peace. Cosmos is also the better pick for a new relationship — marigold's meaning is a bit heavy for three months in.

And if you genuinely can't decide: October is the only month where giving two small pieces makes sense as a concept rather than as indecision. One pearl, one gold-tone, one card explaining that October has two flowers and they got both. We make every piece by hand here in Portugal, so if you want the two to sit well together on the same wrist, send us a message before you order and we'll tell you which lengths match.
If you'd rather move the idea up to the neck, the same logic works with necklaces — pearl at a short 40–42 cm for the cosmos reading, gold-tone at 45 cm or longer for marigold, layered over a jumper.

faq.question: Does October have two birth flowers?
faq.answer: Yes. October's birth flowers are the marigold and the cosmos. Marigold is the older, more traditional of the two and means devotion, warmth and remembrance; cosmos is the gentler one and means order, balance and peace.

faq.question: What is October's birthstone, and does it go with the birth flowers?
faq.answer: October's birthstones are opal and tourmaline. Opal's milky shimmer sits naturally with the white cosmos idea, while pink tourmaline matches pink cosmos. If you want a warm marigold look instead, gold-tone metal is the simpler route.

faq.question: Is the marigold a sad flower?
faq.answer: Not exactly. In Victorian flower language it carried grief and jealousy, but in Mexican and Indian tradition it's a celebration flower — used for Día de los Muertos altars and Diwali garlands. It means strong feeling, which can be love or loss depending on the context.

faq.answer: Yes. Our stainless steel pieces are waterproof and tarnish-resistant, so showering, swimming and rain are all fine. Rinse off sea salt and chlorine afterwards and dry the piece, and it'll keep its finish.

title: Silver Body Chain Outfit Ideas for Autumn 2026
excerpt: Silver body chains are back for fall 2026. Here's how to wear one with jeans, knitwear, slip dresses and party looks — with real lengths and pairings.

content.text: The easiest silver body chain outfits are the ones where the chain does one job: a belly chain sitting just under a cropped knit with low-rise jeans, a layered waist chain worn over a fitted long-sleeve, a shoulder harness across a plain black dress, or a fine hand chain with a rolled-up shirt sleeve. Cool-toned silver is the story for autumn/winter 2026 — Net-a-Porter's PORTER report put it front and centre — and the trick is pairing it with one flash of skin or one thin layer, not five competing pieces. Below are outfits that work right now, in September weather, with clothes you already own.
How do you wear a silver belly chain with jeans?

This is the outfit people search for most, and it's the easiest one to get right. A silver belly chain with jeans works when the waistband sits low enough that the chain rides on skin or just above the denim — not buried under it. Mid-rise and low-rise both work. High-rise works too, but then you wear the chain over the denim, sitting on the waistband like a belt.

For everyday autumn wear, the version that never gets in your way is a single strand. The Silver Belly Chain is plain silver-tone stainless steel, water resistant and anti-tarnish, with a base chain of 71 cm and an open-link extender so you clasp it anywhere along the range. That's the point of a waterproof silver belly chain for everyday — you put it on, shower in it, sleep in it, and stop thinking about it.
Three combinations that hold up in September and October:

items: Straight-leg dark denim + a cropped ribbed knit that ends at the navel + a single silver belly chain. The chain reads as a thin bright line between two heavy textures.
Baggy light-wash jeans + a tucked-in white tank + the chain worn over the waistband. Add a loose grey cardigan you leave open. This is the look that photographs well from the side.
Low-rise jeans + an oversized shirt tied at the waist. The knot sits above the chain, so you see maybe 6 cm of skin and a glint of silver.

content.text: One sizing note, because it's where people go wrong: measure where you actually want the chain to sit, not your trouser size. Waist and hip measurements differ by several centimetres. If you want it low on the hips, measure across the hip bones. Small covers 71–81 cm, Medium 71–91 cm, Large 71–100 cm, and the extender gives you room inside each.
What is a layered silver belly chain outfit, and does it work in winter?

A layered silver belly chain outfit means multiple fine strands at the waist instead of one — either a single multi-strand piece, or two chains stacked at slightly different heights. It reads bolder and catches more light, which is useful in autumn when you're wearing darker, heavier fabrics that swallow a delicate chain.

The Layered Silver Belly Chain does this in one piece: several fine strands that stack and shift as you move. Wear it alone over a black long-sleeve bodysuit with wide trousers, and you've got a whole outfit from one accessory. Or stack it with the plain single-strand chain above for a fuller waist.

Silver body jewellery winter styling comes down to one idea: the chain needs a plain surface to sit against. Ribbed knits, jersey, matte cotton, leather. Avoid busy prints and heavy cable knits — the chain disappears. Some winter pairings that work:

items: Sheer black mesh long-sleeve + layered belly chain underneath the fabric. You see the silver through the mesh, which is warmer than bare skin and just as visible.
Low-slung leather or faux-leather trousers + a cropped black knit + layered chain in the gap.
A slip dress with a thin long-sleeve underneath + a Layered Hip Chain worn over the dress at the hip bones. This is the one for a dinner where you're keeping your coat on until you get inside.
Grey marl sweatpants pulled low + a cropped tee + a single chain. Silver reads well against grey; it's the most forgiving background colour.

content.text: What's the best silver shoulder harness party outfit?

Party season starts in about eight weeks and the shoulder harness is the piece that turns a plain dress into an outfit. The formula: the harness needs a simple neckline and a solid colour. Black, deep green, burgundy, chocolate brown — all the autumn 2026 colours work with silver because silver is cool-toned and doesn't fight them the way yellow gold does.

The Silver Shoulder Harness drapes from the neck across both shoulders and down the chest. It's made for strapless, halter or thin-strap necklines — anything where the shoulders are clear. Over a strapless black column dress it looks structural. Over a plain silk slip it looks softer. What it doesn't work with: high necks, collars, or anything with its own neckline detail.

Sizing matters more here than with a belly chain, because the harness has to sit flat. Neck chains run 34.5 cm (S) to 38 cm (XL), with shoulder chains from 51 cm to 65 cm. If you're between sizes or your shoulders are broader than your neck suggests, message us after ordering and we'll resize it for free. That's not a marketing line — El or Gio will remake it in the studio.

For a bigger statement, the Multi Strand Shoulder Chain gives you more coverage across the chest. That one suits a very plain dress, a bachelorette look, or New Year's Eve. Keep earrings small when you wear either — the harness already occupies the neck and chest, so studs or a thin huggie are enough.
Can you wear silver body jewellery with gold, and how much is too much?

You can mix, but do it on purpose. Mixing works when the two metals are on different parts of the body — silver belly chain, gold rings — or when one piece is deliberately half-and-half. What doesn't work is a silver belly chain with a gold-tone hand chain on the same side of your body in the same photo. It reads as an accident.

With silver dominating this autumn, the simpler route is to go all cool-toned for a season. Silver body chain, silver rings, silver hoops. A Dainty Hand Chain in silver tone with a pushed-up sleeve is the small detail that ties the whole thing together, and at 16.5–20.5 cm on the wrist with a 9 cm connector to the finger, it sits flat enough to wear under a coat.

On quantity, a rule that holds: two chain pieces visible at once, three if one of them is very fine. Belly chain plus hand chain, yes. Belly chain plus shoulder harness plus hand chain plus anklet — that's a costume, not an outfit. Pick the area you want people to look at and put the silver there.
How do you keep a silver body chain looking good through autumn?

Our silver pieces are silver-tone stainless steel, which means they're water resistant and don't tarnish the way sterling does. You can shower in them, swim in them and wear them in the rain — which, given European autumn, matters. Still, a few habits keep the shine sharper for longer:

items: Wipe the chain with a soft dry cloth after a sweaty day or a night out. Body oils and perfume residue dull the finish faster than water does.
Spray perfume and apply body lotion first, then put the chain on. Thirty seconds of patience.
Store it flat in an airtight container or a small zip bag, not tangled in a dish with other jewellery. Fine strands knot fast.
If you're wearing a layered chain under a chunky knit all day, take it off before bed — friction against wool is the main thing that scuffs a fine link.
Coming back from the beach or a pool, rinse with fresh water. Chlorine and salt won't ruin it, but rinsing takes ten seconds.

faq.answer: Silver. Net-a-Porter's PORTER 2026 report flagged cool-toned silver jewellery as the dominant direction for fall/winter 2026. Gold-tone still works, especially with warm-toned autumn colours, but silver is the one getting styled everywhere right now.

faq.answer: Yes, and a lot of people do. A single fine chain sits flat under a t-shirt or knit and nobody sees it, which is why waterproof stainless steel matters — you can leave it on for weeks. Layered multi-strand chains are bulkier and better worn visibly.

title: October Birthstone Meaning: Opal and Tourmaline
excerpt: October has two birthstones. Opal means hope, creativity and loyalty. Tourmaline means protection and emotional balance. Here's how to choose between them.

content.text: October has two birthstones: opal and tourmaline. Opal stands for hope, creativity, loyalty and imagination — its shifting colours have been linked to inspiration since Roman times. Tourmaline stands for protection, calm and emotional balance, and because it comes in more colours than any other gemstone, it's often called the stone that matches any mood.

If you're shopping for an October birthday right now, that's the short answer. Below is the longer one: where each meaning comes from, which stone suits which person, what they cost, and how to wear them without ruining them.
Why does October have two birthstones?

Opal is the old one. It appears on birthstone lists going back centuries, and the Romans called it opalus — a stone they believed held the colours of every other gem at once. Pliny the Elder wrote that opal combined the fire of ruby, the purple of amethyst and the green of emerald in one stone. That's where the creativity and imagination meaning comes from: a stone that refuses to be one colour.

Tourmaline was added in 1952, when the American jewellery trade updated the official birthstone list. The reason was practical. Fine opal is fragile, expensive and hard to source in matching sets, so the trade wanted a second October stone that was tougher, easier to find and available in a wide price range. Tourmaline fit perfectly. It's been on the list ever since, which is why modern charts show both.
So neither is more correct. Opal is the traditional October birthstone, tourmaline is the modern one, and both are fully official. Pick on meaning, colour or budget.
What does opal mean, and what do the colours symbolise?

Opal's core meaning is hope and faithfulness. In the Middle Ages it was tied to loyalty — a gift between close friends or lovers meant to say you're constant. Bedouin tradition held that opals caught lightning and fell from the sky during storms. Later folklore added inspiration and creative work, which is why writers, artists and anyone starting something new tend to like it as a gift.

The play of colour matters too. White opal with blue and green flashes reads calm and dreamy. Fire opal, which runs orange to red, is linked to energy and courage. Black opal, the rarest kind, is associated with protection and is the most expensive per carat. If someone in your life has an October birthday and loves milky blues, a white opal is the obvious route — and a pale, watery Layered Turquoise Bead Bracelet at €24 sits beside opal tones beautifully if you want a second bracelet to stack with it.

One more thing worth knowing: the superstition that opals bring bad luck is nonsense and it has a traceable source. Sir Walter Scott's 1829 novel Anne of Geierstein featured a cursed opal, sales in Europe crashed, and the story stuck. Before that book, opal was considered one of the luckiest stones you could own.
What does tourmaline mean, and what does each colour stand for?

Tourmaline's name comes from the Sinhalese toramalli, meaning mixed-coloured stones. That's the whole idea. A single crystal can shift from pink at one end to green at the other — those are called watermelon tourmalines, and they're the most collected type. The general meaning across all colours is protection and emotional steadiness.
Because the colours vary so widely, people usually pick by shade:
What the main tourmaline colours are said to mean:
items: Pink tourmaline — compassion, gentleness and heart-healing. This is the most common choice for October birthday jewellery and the one you'll see in most birthstone bracelets.
Green tourmaline (verdelite) — growth, vitality and new starts. Good for someone moving house, changing careers or finishing a degree.
Black tourmaline (schorl) — grounding and protection. The one people keep on a desk or wear daily when life is loud.
Blue tourmaline (indicolite) — clear communication and honesty. Rarer, so expect a higher price.
Watermelon tourmaline — balance between heart and head. The pink-and-green crystal, usually cut in slices so you can see both colours.

content.text: Tourmaline also has a party trick: it's pyroelectric and piezoelectric, meaning it builds a static charge when heated or squeezed. Dutch traders in the 1700s used warm tourmaline crystals to pull ash out of their pipes. That property is part of why the stone picked up its protective reputation.
Which October birthstone should you choose — opal or tourmaline?
Practical differences decide this more than meaning does. Here's the honest breakdown.
Choose based on how they'll wear it:
items: For everyday wear — tourmaline. It sits at 7 to 7.5 on the Mohs hardness scale, similar to quartz. It handles a normal day of typing, cooking and bag straps without scratching.
For someone who never takes jewellery off — tourmaline again, on a stainless steel chain. Steel is waterproof and tarnish-resistant, so showers and sea swims aren't a problem.
For a special-occasion or evening piece — opal. It's softer, 5.5 to 6.5, and contains water, so it's happiest on a piece that comes off at the end of the night.
For a romantic gift — pink tourmaline. Compassion and the heart is the clearest meaning of the set, and pink flatters most skin tones.
For a creative person or someone starting over — opal. Hope and imagination is exactly the message.
On a tight budget — synthetic or lab-created opal gives you the full colour play for a fraction of the price, and it's harder than natural opal.

content.text: If the person already owns a lot of jewellery, skip the stone debate and go personal instead. October's birth flowers are the marigold and the cosmos, and a Birth Flower Charm Bracelet at €28 says the same thing as a birthstone without competing with what they already wear. Or go with their letter on a Pearl Heart Initial Bracelet, also €28.
How do you care for opal and tourmaline jewellery?

Opal is the one that needs rules. It holds between 3 and 21 percent water, so dry heat, sudden temperature changes and harsh chemicals can cause crazing — fine cracks across the surface that can't be repaired. Take opal off before showering, swimming, cleaning, or sitting in strong sun on a terrace. Clean it with a soft damp cloth only. Never use an ultrasonic cleaner or steam. Store it away from harder stones so nothing scratches it, and if you're storing it for months, a slightly humid spot beats a bone-dry drawer.

Tourmaline is far easier. Warm water, mild soap, soft brush, dry properly. Avoid ultrasonic cleaners anyway, since many tourmalines have internal inclusions that don't like vibration. Keep it out of prolonged direct sunlight, which can fade some pinks over years.

The setting matters as much as the stone. A stainless steel chain won't tarnish, won't turn your wrist green and won't react to sweat or sunscreen, which means the only thing you have to think about is the stone itself. Gold-tone steel gives you the warm look without the maintenance of plated brass.
What to pair with October birthstone jewellery

Opal's milky blues and tourmaline's pinks both sit well against pearl. A soft stack reads better than one loud piece, especially on a smaller wrist. Two or three bracelets at 17 to 19 cm, one with stone, one with pearl, one plain chain — that's the formula that works in photos and in real life.

title: What Jewellery to Wear With a Strapless Dress
excerpt: Strapless dress, bare shoulders — here's exactly what necklace length, shoulder chain or bicep chain to wear, with real measurements and party-season pairings.

content.text: With a strapless dress, put your jewellery where the dress stops: the collarbone, the shoulders and the upper arm. A short necklace (40–45 cm) sitting on bare skin, a shoulder chain draped across the top of the chest, or a bicep chain on one arm will all read as intentional — pick one as your main piece and keep the rest small. Long pendants and heavy chokers tend to fight a straight neckline, so skip those unless the dress is very plain.

It's late September, party dresses are back in shop windows across Europe, and the strapless cut is everywhere again. The problem is always the same: a whole lot of bare skin from your ears to the top of the dress, and no straps to break it up. Below is how we'd fill that space — with sizes, lengths and pairings, not vague advice.
What necklace length for a strapless neckline?

A straight-across (bandeau) neckline draws a hard horizontal line. Your necklace should either sit clearly above that line or be long enough to drop well below it. Anything that lands right on the edge of the fabric looks like a mistake.
Lengths that work, measured end to end:
items: 35–38 cm (choker): sits high on the neck. Good with a sweetheart neckline or a dress with a bit of volume up top. Keep it thin — a wide choker plus bare shoulders can feel heavy. A slim piece like the Pink Cross Choker Necklace works because the colour does the talking, not the bulk.
and

40–45 cm (princess): the safest length for a strapless dress. It lands on the collarbone or just below, filling the gap without touching the fabric. This is where most pendant necklaces sit, including the Birth Flower Charm Necklace.
50–55 cm (matinee): drops onto the dress itself. Only do this if the fabric is matte and plain — on sequins or lace it disappears.
70 cm+ (opera): skip it with strapless. It swings, it tangles, and it pulls the eye down away from your shoulders.

content.text: One more rule of thumb: if your dress has a straight neckline, a V-shaped or pendant necklace softens it. If the neckline is a sweetheart curve, a simple round chain follows the shape better than a pendant.
Is a shoulder chain for a strapless dress too much?

Not if it's the only statement you wear. A shoulder chain is the piece strapless dresses were waiting for — it gives you the strap line you're missing without covering anything up, and it moves when you move.

If you're wearing a shoulder chain or harness, go with studs or small huggies. Your neck and shoulder area is already doing the work. Keep wrists nearly bare — one thin bracelet at most.

title: How to Wear a Toggle Necklace: Front Clasp Styling Tips
excerpt: Wear a toggle necklace with the clasp at the front, not hidden at the back. Here's how to fasten it, what length to pick, and how to layer it in autumn.

content.text: Wear a toggle necklace with the clasp at the front, centred on your collarbone. The T-bar and ring are part of the design, not something to hide at the back of your neck. Keep the neckline simple, leave the middle of your chest clear, and let the clasp do the talking.

That's the short answer. The longer one covers how to fasten it on your own, what chain length sits where, and how to layer it without the toggle disappearing behind another chain. Below is everything you'd want to know before you wear one out.
How do you fasten a toggle clasp by yourself?
A toggle clasp (sometimes written OT clasp, for the O ring and T bar) closes by gravity, not by a spring. Most people fumble it the first time, then never think about it again.
Here's the order that works:
items: Bring both ends round to the front, below your chin, where you can see them.
Hold the O ring flat between your thumb and finger, opening facing you.
Slide the T bar through the ring lengthwise, pointing it straight into the hole. It only fits one way.
Push the bar all the way through until the chain behind it passes the ring, then let go.
The bar turns sideways on its own and sits across the ring. Gently tug both sides to check it has seated flat.
Rotate the whole chain until the clasp sits in the dip at the base of your throat, or just to one side if you prefer it off-centre.

content.text: If the bar keeps slipping back out, you're probably not pushing it far enough through. The little link between the bar and the chain needs to clear the ring completely. And if you're wearing something with a pendant hanging off the clasp itself, the weight of the pendant helps hold everything in place once it's through.
What length toggle necklace should you get?

A 40cm chain is the sweet spot for a front-clasp necklace. It lands on or just below the collarbone on most people, which is exactly where you want a toggle so it's visible above a crew neck and doesn't vanish into a shirt.

For reference, 35–38cm is choker territory, sitting snug at the base of the neck. 40–42cm rests at the collarbone. 45cm drops a few centimetres lower onto the chest, and 50cm and up sits over a t-shirt or jumper. Toggles look their best at 40–45cm because you need a little slack for the clasp to hang properly. Too tight and the bar sits at an angle; too long and the whole thing slides sideways when you move.

The Chunky Toggle Cross Necklace is a good example of the proportions working together: a bold rolo link chain at 40cm, with a 3.5cm x 2cm cross hanging straight off the front toggle. That means the cross drops below the collarbone even though the chain itself sits at it, so you get visible length without a long chain. It's €30 in gold tone or silver tone, stainless steel, and weighs around 10g, so it doesn't drag on your neck through a full day.

If you'd rather go softer than a cross, the Chunky Pearl Heart Toggle Necklace works the same way: imitation pearl beads, with a gold rope-trim heart hanging straight off the front toggle. It's €30, stainless steel with 18k gold plating and hypoallergenic, and the pearls make it an easy one to wear over a black knit or a crisp white shirt.

If your neck measures more than about 37cm and you want a 40cm chain to sit low rather than close, look for an extender or size up to 45cm. A chain that's slightly too short will keep pulling the clasp off-centre.
How do you layer a toggle necklace with other necklaces?

The rule with toggles is simple: don't put anything across the clasp. The whole point is that the front closure is visible, so any second necklace should sit clearly above or clearly below it, with at least 4–5cm of gap.
Three pairings that work:
items: Choker above, toggle below. A short piece at 35–38cm sits high on the neck and leaves the collarbone clear. The Birth Month Teardrop Choker at €20 does this well — the small teardrop stays up near the throat, so it never fights with a chunky chain underneath.

Match the motif, change the scale. If you like a cross, wearing two isn't too much as long as they're different sizes and lengths. The Pink Cross Choker Necklace at €28 is delicate and sits high; a heavier cross on a bold chain below it reads as deliberate rather than accidental.
Add colour, keep the metal quiet. A beaded piece like the Colorful Crystal Bead Choker at €24 brings texture without adding another metal chain to the mix, which stops the layers looking busy.

content.text: Two layers is usually enough with a chunky toggle. Three works only if the third is very fine and sits well below, around 50cm. And if you're mixing gold tone and silver tone on purpose, keep it to two pieces so it reads as a choice.
What necklines work with a toggle necklace in autumn?
Now that jumpers are back out, the necklines change and so does where the necklace sits. A front-clasp chain needs a bit of open skin or a clean edge to work against.

A crew neck knit is the easiest. A 40cm chain sits just at or above the ribbed edge, and the pendant rests on the knit. Pick a plain colour — heavy cable knits swallow chains. An open shirt or a flannel with the top two buttons undone gives you a natural frame; let the toggle sit where the collar opens. A zip-neck or half-zip sweatshirt works too, with the zip pulled down a few centimetres.

With a turtleneck, wear the necklace over the fabric rather than under it. A chunky chain on a fine black roll neck is one of the best autumn looks there is, and it stops the chain rubbing against your skin all day. If you're going out in the evening, a scoop or square neck top with a single bold chain needs nothing else — no second necklace, no big earrings.

One thing to watch: crossbody bag straps. A strap sitting over your chest can shift a toggle and, over a long day, work it loose. Either put the bag on the opposite shoulder or wear the chain under your coat while you're moving around. It's also worth noting that chunky toggle chains are genuinely unisex — the design isn't gendered, and a 40cm chain sits well on most necks regardless.
Do toggle clasps come undone, and how do you look after one?

Toggles hold well when the necklace has some weight to it, because that weight keeps constant downward tension on the bar. Very light, fine toggle chains are the ones that pop open. A chunky rolo link at around 10g is heavy enough to stay put through a normal day, and a pendant hanging from the clasp adds to that.

Still, glance down and check it now and then, especially after pulling a jumper over your head or taking off a scarf. If you ever find the bar has worked its way partly through, just push it back and let it settle flat.

Care is straightforward with stainless steel. It's waterproof and tarnish-resistant, so rain on the walk home, a wet coat collar or a sink of washing-up won't ruin it. Wipe it gently with a soft cloth after each wear to lift off sweat, perfume and body lotion — that's what dulls the shine, not the metal itself. Store it in an airtight container or a small zip bag when you're not wearing it, and keep chunky chains separate so they don't scratch finer pieces.
Perfume and hairspray go on first, necklace second. Give the perfume a minute to dry. That one habit keeps a chain looking new for years.

Everything in our necklaces range is made by hand here in our studio, which means slight variations between pieces are normal — no two are exactly identical. Orders dispatch within 1–2 business days, so if you're buying for something coming up, order with a week's breathing room.

faq.answer: You can, but you lose the main feature of the design — the T-bar and ring are meant to be seen. Turning it to the back also means any pendant attached to the clasp ends up behind your neck instead of on your chest.

faq.answer: Yes. A bold chain with a front toggle at around 40cm sits well on most necks and the design isn't gendered. Choosing gold tone or silver tone usually matters more for how it looks than the style itself.

title: Birthday Jewelry She'll Actually Wear Every Day

Skip the Delicate — Go for Durable

Think about her style first. If she's minimal, go for something sleek and simple. If she's bohemian, lean into chains and layering. If she's maximalist, she'll love pieces that can be mixed and stacked. The right piece feels like an extension of who she already is, not a push in a new direction.

title: Gold vs Silver Body Jewelry: How to Choose
excerpt: The real difference between gold and silver jewelry—and which one actually works for your skin and style.

content.text: You're scrolling through body jewelry and you see it: the same piece in both gold and silver. So which one do you actually pick? It's not just about what looks pretty on the screen. The choice comes down to your skin tone, your existing jewelry, and honestly, how the metal feels against your skin.

Here's the thing—gold and silver are completely different metals, and they interact with your skin in different ways. Neither one is objectively "better." But one will almost always look better on you, and when you find it, you'll notice the difference immediately.
Does your skin tone matter?

Yes, but not in the way you think. It's less about whether you have warm or cool undertones and more about what you're already wearing. Look at your wrists right now. What color metal do you see on your existing rings, watches, or bracelets? That's your answer. Your jewelry should talk to each other, not fight.

If you're building a collection from scratch, gold tends to feel warmer and softer, while silver reads as cooler and more modern. Neither will look "wrong" on any skin tone—it's about personal preference and what makes you feel like yourself. Try holding both up to your wrist in natural light before you decide.
What about mixing gold and silver?

Mixing metals used to be considered a fashion rule-break. Now? It's completely normal. The trick is intentionality. If you're layering a Dainty Gold Body Chain with a silver belly chain, they should work together visually—not just happen to exist on your body at the same time.

The easiest way to make mixed metals work is to give them different jobs. Wear gold as your base layer and silver as an accent, or vice versa. Or keep them on different areas—a gold choker and silver anklets, for example. When metals have breathing room, they enhance each other instead of clashing.
What about your daily life and skin sensitivity?

Here's something people don't talk about enough: how the metal feels on your skin over time. All of our body jewelry is made from high-quality stainless steel that's waterproof and tarnish-resistant, so durability isn't the issue. What matters is whether you like the feeling of gold or silver against your body, especially if you're wearing it all day.

Some people find that one metal sits better against their skin or stays cooler or just feels more like "them." The only way to know is to try it. If you're ordering from us, keep track of which metal you reach for most. That's the one that works for you. Whether you're choosing a Turquoise Enamel Bead Double Choker or a Pearl Lariat Back Necklace, the metal should feel like an extension of you, not something you're constantly aware of.

So here's the real answer: pick the metal that matches what you're already wearing, that feels good on your skin, and that makes you want to put it on. That's not overthinking it—that's knowing yourself. The best jewelry is the piece you actually want to wear.

title: Gold Plated vs Gold Tone: What Actually Lasts Longer
excerpt: One sounds fancier, but they're completely different. Here's what you need to know before buying.

content.text: You've probably seen both terms thrown around when shopping for jewelry. Gold plated. Gold tone. They sound similar enough that you might think they're the same thing with different marketing. They're not. Understanding the difference matters because it directly affects how long your jewelry lasts and how it ages.

Let's cut through the confusion. We make body jewelry that's meant to be worn every day — in the shower, at the beach, through life. So we've thought a lot about durability. Here's what actually separates these two.
What gold plated actually means

Gold plating is a real process. A thin layer of actual gold is bonded to a base metal underneath — usually stainless steel or brass. That gold layer is typically between 0.5 to 2.5 microns thick. It's real gold sitting on top of something else.

The catch? That thin gold layer wears away over time. Friction, sweat, soap, chlorine — they all speed up the process. You might get 6-18 months of regular wear before the plating starts to fade or chip. After that, you're seeing the base metal underneath, and the magic is gone. Gold plating isn't repairable on handmade pieces like ours, so once it wears, it's done.
What gold tone actually is

Gold tone is just stainless steel (or another metal) that's been colored or finished to look gold. No actual gold involved. It's painted on, basically. Think of it like the difference between a gold-painted wall and a wall covered in gold leaf.

Here's the real advantage: gold tone doesn't chip or peel the way plating does. The color is part of the metal itself. It can fade or dull slightly over years of wear, but it doesn't suddenly reveal a completely different metal underneath. You get more consistent wear, even if the shine dulls eventually.

We work exclusively with high-quality stainless steel that's waterproof and tarnish-resistant. It's built to handle daily life — showers, sweat, salt water, everything. Browse our full shop all body jewelry collection and you'll notice we don't do gold plating. We chose durability over that initial gleam.
Which one should you actually choose

If you love the look of gold and want something you can wear constantly without thinking about maintenance, gold tone is the smarter choice. It lasts longer without the heartbreak of watching it peel. If you want actual gold on your skin and don't mind replacing a piece every year or so, gold plating works — just go in knowing the timeline.

The pieces we make — like our Birthstone Ring — are designed to be part of your everyday. You wear them to the beach. You shower in them. You sleep in them. That's why we built them to last without the fuss of gold plating wearing away. Real materials, real durability, no surprises.

faq.question: Is gold plated jewelry real gold?
faq.answer: Yes, the outer layer is real gold, but it's extremely thin (less than 3 microns). The base underneath is a different metal, usually stainless steel or brass. Over time with regular wear, that thin gold layer wears away and exposes the base metal beneath it.

faq.question: How long does gold plated jewelry last?
faq.answer: With regular wear, gold plating typically lasts 6-18 months before you start seeing fading or chipping. The timeline depends on how often you wear it, whether you expose it to water and sweat, and the thickness of the plating. Heavy daily wear speeds up the process significantly.

faq.question: Does gold tone jewelry fade?
faq.answer: Gold tone can fade or dull slightly over years of heavy wear because the color is a surface finish, not the material itself. However, it won't chip or peel the way plating does — it degrades gradually rather than suddenly revealing a different metal underneath.

title: Mix Gold and Silver Jewelry Without the Doubt

content.text: You've probably heard it before: gold and silver don't mix. But that rule is outdated, and honestly? It was never really a rule at all. The truth is simpler than you think — mixing metals is about intention, not restriction. Your wrists and neck can absolutely handle both, and when you do it right, they look better for it.

The key isn't to avoid one metal or stick rigidly to one tone. It's to think about balance and what actually works with your skin. Once you understand that, you'll feel confident wearing whatever combination feels right to you.
Start with your skin tone

Your skin naturally leans warm or cool, and that's the foundation for mixing metals confidently. If you have warm undertones (golden, peachy), gold will feel more natural next to your skin — but silver can still work beautifully as an accent. If you're cool-toned (pink, red undertones), silver tends to feel closer to your natural palette, but gold adds warmth and interest.

The thing is: you don't have to choose just one. Cool-toned skin can absolutely wear gold. Warm-toned skin looks amazing in silver. The difference is in how you balance them. Think of it like wearing outfits — you're creating harmony, not following a rigid dress code.
The balance rule: lead with one, accent with the other

Here's the practical framework that makes mixing metals actually easy. Pick one metal as your main player — the one that dominates your look. That's usually your watch, your go-to necklace, or your main bracelet. Let that metal be 60-70% of what you're wearing. Then, use the second metal in smaller, secondary pieces. One delicate accent piece. One thin chain. One charm or detail.

For example: wear a gold Goddess Shoulder Chain as your statement piece, then add a silver Dainty Summer Belly Chain underneath. The gold leads; the silver whispers. No conflict. No confusion. Just intention.

This approach works everywhere — your hands, your neck, your body. One metal takes the spotlight. The other adds depth. When you have that visual hierarchy, your eye sees a complete look instead of a clash.
Where to layer without overthinking it

Layering is where people get most nervous about mixing metals, but it's actually one of the easiest places to do it. Wear your gold necklace at your collarbone, then layer a thinner silver chain below it. The different lengths keep them visually separate, so mixing metals becomes an asset instead of a worry. Each chain gets its own space.

The same works for your wrists and body. A gold bracelet with a silver body chain doesn't compete — they occupy different visual zones. Stack a Pearl Lariat Back Necklace in silver with gold body jewelry, and suddenly the mix feels intentional and balanced instead of accidental.

The real freedom here? You get to build layers that actually feel like you, not layers that follow some invisible rulebook. Mix metals the way you mix your outfits — with confidence and your own taste as the guide.

title: Gold Plated vs Gold Tone: What You Actually Need to Know
excerpt: One lasts years. One won't. Here's how to tell the difference—and which one's actually worth your money.

content.text: You're scrolling through jewelry and you see two pieces that look identical. One says "gold plated." The other says "gold tone." They cost different amounts. You have no idea which one to pick. If that sounds familiar, you're not alone—and the difference between these two terms matters way more than most people realize.

Here's the thing: these aren't just different words for the same thing. One is an actual layer of real gold. The other is basically paint. Knowing which is which will save you from buying jewelry that tarnishes in three months or investing in something that'll actually last.
What gold plated actually is

Gold plating is a real process. A thin layer of genuine gold is bonded to a base metal (usually copper or brass) using electricity. That layer is typically between 0.5 to 2.5 microns thick—thin enough that it costs way less than solid gold, but thick enough to actually be gold.

The upside: it looks like real gold and it'll stay that way for a while. How long? If you take care of it—avoid constant water, sweat, and friction—a quality gold-plated piece can last 1-3 years. Some last longer. Eventually, the layer wears through and you'll see the base metal underneath, but you get real value out of it first.
What gold tone is (and why it's different)

Gold tone is just a description. It means the metal is colored or painted to look gold. There's no actual gold in the plating process—just a coating applied to make it gold-colored. It's cheaper, faster, and it shows.

Here's the reality: gold tone jewelry will tarnish, fade, and chip much faster. We're talking months, not years. Once it starts to wear, it peels, flakes, or discolors unevenly. And there's no "real gold" underneath—just base metal that will eventually oxidize or discolor.
This doesn't mean gold tone is always a bad choice. If you want something fun and temporary for €15, go for it. But if you're looking for jewelry you'll actually wear regularly, it's not the move.
Why we skip both—and what we do instead

At Bodystrands, we don't do gold plating or gold tone. We work with high-quality stainless steel instead. It's waterproof, it doesn't tarnish, and it genuinely lasts through everyday wear—swimming, showers, gym sessions, all of it.

Stainless steel has a bright, clean aesthetic that works with almost any look. It's different from gold, sure, but it's honest about what it is. You get a piece that's built to last, made by hand in our Portuguese studio, at prices that won't hurt your wallet. Whether you're drawn to something like our Monogram Letter Necklace or exploring our full body jewelry collection, you know exactly what you're getting and how long it'll actually stick around.

The real difference between gold plated and gold tone comes down to this: one is real gold (that'll eventually wear off), one is fake gold (that'll fall apart faster). Neither needs to be your only option. Pick the material that matches how you actually live—and wear your jewelry without worrying.

title: How to Store Body Jewelry So It Actually Lasts
excerpt: Keep your chains looking brand new. Here's exactly how to store them—no complicated steps needed.

content.text: You invested in a piece you love. Maybe it's a Script Initial Bracelet with your initial, or a Zodiac Belly Chain that actually means something to you. So it makes sense to keep it looking as good as the day it arrived. The good news: storing body jewelry properly isn't hard. It just takes a few intentional habits.

All of our pieces are made from high-quality stainless steel, which means they're built to handle everyday wear, water, and sweat without tarnishing or corroding. That durability is real. But storage still matters. How you keep your jewelry when you're not wearing it determines whether it stays pristine or starts to look dull or tangled.
The basics: dry, cool, away from humidity

Start with the fundamentals. Store your jewelry in a cool, dry place—a bedroom drawer is ideal. Moisture and humidity are the biggest threats to any metal, even stainless steel. If you live somewhere humid or you like to keep jewelry in a bathroom, rethink it. Condensation builds up over time, and that's when you'll start seeing things you don't want to see.

Keep pieces away from direct sunlight, extreme heat, and temperature swings. Don't store them near a radiator, heater, or windowsill where the sun hits all day. Stable conditions mean stable jewelry. Simple as that.

If you're storing multiple pieces together, make sure they're not in a pile or tangled in a box. Chains, especially longer ones like Bridal Hair Vine Chains, can get knotted around each other. That doesn't damage them, but it's annoying to untangle.
Keep them separated and organized

The easiest method is to use small pouches, compartments, or even ziplock bags—one piece per bag. This prevents tangling, keeps dust off, and makes it easy to grab exactly what you want. You don't need anything fancy. A fabric jewelry box with dividers works. So does a drawer organizer with small sections.

If you wear pieces regularly—like a Pearl Glasses Chain or a daily bracelet—keep it somewhere visible and easy to reach instead of buried. The more accessible something is, the more likely you'll actually wear it instead of letting it sit forgotten.

For delicate or sentimental pieces, consider a small box or padded pouch that you keep in a drawer or shelf. These are the pieces you're saving or wearing for special occasions. They deserve a little extra care.
Before you store it: clean and dry

Always clean your jewelry before storing it, especially if you've been wearing it all day or after swimming or working out. Sweat, salt water, and chlorine can leave residue that builds up over time. A quick rinse under lukewarm water and a gentle dry with a soft cloth is all you need. Make sure it's completely dry before putting it away—no moisture lingering.

If there's visible buildup or it just needs a deeper clean, use a soft toothbrush or microfiber cloth. You're not doing anything aggressive here. Stainless steel is tough, but gentle handling keeps everything looking its best. Once it's dry, it's ready to go in its storage spot.

That's really it. Dry storage, separated pieces, stable temperature, and a quick clean before you put things away. Your jewelry will stay looking new, won't tangle, and will be ready to wear whenever you want it. El and Gio make each piece by hand for you—treating it right means it'll last.

title: Keep Your Body Jewelry Looking New: Storage Tips That Work
excerpt: Your favorite chains deserve better than a tangled drawer. Here's how to store them so they stay beautiful.

Start with a dry environment. Moisture is the enemy of jewelry longevity, even with high-quality stainless steel that resists tarnish. Keep your pieces in a cool, dry spot away from bathrooms and kitchen sinks. If you live somewhere humid, consider a small dehumidifier or silica gel packets in your storage space. This simple step prevents most damage before it even starts.

Separate your pieces so they don't tangle or scratch each other. A drawer organizer with small compartments works perfectly. If you prefer hanging storage, a jewelry stand or wall hooks keep everything visible and untangled. The Layered Body Chain and delicate pieces especially benefit from being stored separately—they're too beautiful to spend half your morning untangling.

Avoid storing jewelry in plastic bags or boxes without ventilation for long periods. Plastic can trap moisture and potentially react with the metal over time. Use soft cloth pouches or cardboard boxes with tissue paper instead. If a piece came with packaging, that's often ideal for long-term storage.

Keep your jewelry away from direct sunlight and heat sources. Sunlight doesn't damage stainless steel the way it might other metals, but it's still good practice to store in shade. Heat can weaken any adhesive used in charm attachments or gemstone settings, so keep pieces away from radiators, heaters, and warm windowsills.

If you wear your body jewelry daily—which is exactly what high-quality stainless steel is built for—clean it occasionally before storing. A soft cloth is all you need. For pieces like our Pearl Hand Chain or any personalised charm pieces, a gentle wipe removes oils and keeps everything looking pristine. Let it air dry completely before putting it away.

Don't overcrowd your storage space. When jewelry sits too tightly packed, it gets bent, kinked, or damaged. Give each piece room to breathe. This is especially true for delicate chains and layered pieces—they need space to stay in their intended shape. A well-organized drawer might actually hold fewer pieces than you think, but they'll stay perfect.

Check your stored jewelry every few months. A quick look lets you spot any issues early and reminds you of pieces you haven't worn in a while. Rotate what you wear regularly. This spreads the wear across your collection and keeps everything feeling new. Because here's the truth: jewelry made with care deserves to be worn and loved, not locked away forever.

title: How to Tell if Your Jewelry is Truly Waterproof

The material matters more than anything else. Stainless steel—specifically it—is genuinely waterproof because it doesn't rust or tarnish when exposed to water, salt water, or chlorine. Coatings and sealants are temporary fixes, not real solutions. You'll see jewelry treated with clear lacquer, resin, or other protective layers marketed as waterproof. The problem? Those coatings wear off. They chip, flake, and fade. Within months or a year, you're back to exposed metal that tarnishes. This is especially true for pieces you wear daily—like body chains or anklets that get constant friction and contact.

Check the clasp and closures too. A waterproof chain means nothing if the clasp corrodes or breaks after a few weeks. Look for solid stainless steel hardware throughout—not just the chain itself. Every connector, jump ring, and fastening point should match the same quality standard. This is where many brands cut corners, and it's where your jewelry fails first.

The Waterproof Belly Chain is waterproof because every single component—chain, hardware, closures—is high-quality stainless steel. No coatings. No gimmicks. It'll survive saltwater swims, daily showers, and years of wear without tarnishing or corroding. That's what true waterproof looks like.

Real talk: if a brand can't tell you the exact material or grade of steel used, walk away. Transparency matters. You should know exactly what you're buying and why it works. Vague descriptions like 'water-resistant' or 'treated for moisture' are red flags. They're admitting the piece isn't actually waterproof—just less likely to fall apart immediately.

Your lifestyle determines what you actually need. If you wear body jewelry daily—to the beach, in the shower, while swimming—you need genuine high-quality stainless steel. title: Gold Plated vs Gold Tone: What Actually Matters
excerpt: One lasts years. One lasts weeks. Here's how to tell the difference and why it matters for your jewelry.
content: You've probably seen both terms thrown around in jewelry listings. Gold plated. Gold tone. They sound similar enough, right? Wrong. There's actually a massive difference between them, and knowing the distinction will save you money and frustration.

Gold tone is basically paint. It's a thin coating of gold-colored finish applied to base metal — usually brass or stainless steel — through an electroplating process. The coating is so thin (often just a few microns) that it starts wearing off pretty quickly. Rub it the wrong way, sweat on it, shower in it, and you'll see the base metal peeking through within weeks or months.

Gold plating is thicker than gold tone, but not by much. It's still electroplated, but the gold layer is typically 2.5 microns or more — which sounds tiny, but makes a real difference. A properly plated piece will last you 1-3 years with regular wear, depending on how much you're actually wearing it and how you care for it.

Here's the thing: neither gold plating nor gold tone is permanent. They're both designed to wear away eventually. That's just physics. Your body chemistry, your daily habits, even the products you use — they all speed up the process. If you're wearing a gold-plated piece constantly, sweating in it, sleeping in it, showering with it, you're going to see wear faster than someone who takes it off before bed.

So why do brands use these methods at all? Cost and accessibility. Real solid gold jewelry is expensive. Gold plating lets you wear the look you love without breaking the bank. But you need to go in with eyes open about what you're getting and how long it will realistically last.

We chose a different route at Bodystrands. Every piece we make uses high-quality stainless steel — no plating, no coating, no finish that wears away. It's waterproof, it won't tarnish, and you can wear it every single day without worrying about it degrading. Whether you're grabbing our Eyeglasses Chain or the Boho Beach Body Chain, the material stays exactly the same year after year.

If you do choose plated jewelry, here's how to make it last: take it off before you shower, before you sleep, and definitely before you swim or hit the gym. Avoid lotions and perfumes on the areas where the jewelry touches your skin. Store it in a dry place. These habits sound strict, but they genuinely extend the life of the piece.

At the end of the day, it comes down to what you want from your jewelry. If you like switching pieces constantly and don't mind replacing them, plated jewelry is fine. If you want something you can throw on every morning and forget about, reach for durable materials that are built to last. Your wallet and your wrists will thank you.

title: Can You Shower With Body Jewelry On? The Real Answer
excerpt: Yes, you can—but there's a right way to do it. Here's what you need to know about keeping your pieces safe.
content: The short answer: yes, you can shower with your body jewelry on. But before you relax completely, there's a difference between *can* and *should*, and it matters for keeping your pieces looking beautiful for years.

When we make each piece here in our Portuguese studio, we choose high-quality stainless steel for one reason: it's built to handle real life. This grade of steel is waterproof, tarnish-resistant, and designed for everyday wear—including showers. You're not going to damage the metal itself by getting it wet.

What you *do* need to think about is what else is in your shower. Shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and especially chlorinated water can leave residue on your jewelry that builds up over time. Even though it won't rust or tarnish, that buildup can make your pieces look dull and cloudy. Here's our honest advice: rinse your jewelry under cool water if you shower with it on. Skip the soap and shampoo directly on your chains. The cooler water won't hurt anything, but it won't stress the metal or any delicate details either. It's the smallest difference that keeps your pieces looking new.

After your shower, dry your jewelry with a soft cloth. Water sitting on metal for hours can cause spotting, even with high-quality stainless steel. A quick pat-dry takes 30 seconds and makes a real difference. If you notice any buildup, a gentle wipe with a damp cloth and mild soap does the job—just avoid scrubbing.

title: How to Clean Your Stainless Steel Jewelry at Home
excerpt: Your body jewelry deserves care, not confusion. Here's exactly how to keep it looking new.
content: You bought stainless steel for a reason — it's built to last through sweat, showers, and real life. But even the best material needs a little attention to stay brilliant. The good news? Cleaning your pieces takes maybe five minutes and nothing you don't already have at home.

Start with warm water and mild dish soap. This is your go-to for regular maintenance, especially after workouts or beach days. Just grab a soft cloth or old toothbrush, work the soapy water gently over every part of your jewelry, then rinse thoroughly under clean running water. Dry it completely with a lint-free cloth — this step matters because water spots can dull the shine.

For pieces like our Layered Pearl Bracelet or any jewelry with delicate details, the soft toothbrush is your best friend. The bristles get into crevices without scratching the metal. Just be gentle around any stone settings or pearl elements, and you're good.

If your jewelry needs deeper cleaning, white vinegar works surprisingly well. Soak your pieces in white vinegar for 15 to 30 minutes, then brush gently with a soft cloth. The acid cuts through buildup without being harsh on stainless steel. Rinse with clean water and dry completely.

Baking soda is another solid option for stubborn spots. Mix it with a little water to make a paste, apply it gently to the affected area, let it sit for a few minutes, then rinse and dry. This method is especially useful if your Cross Belly Chain or any layered piece has picked up tarnish or discoloration.

Avoid harsh chemicals, bleach, and abrasive scrubbers. Stainless steel is tough, but these can still damage the finish or leave scratches. Keep your cleaning approach simple — you really don't need anything fancy. And never use a microfiber cloth on these pieces; stick with soft cotton or linen instead.

Storage matters too. Keep your jewelry in a dry place, away from humidity if possible. If you wear your pieces daily, you probably don't need to store them at all — just give them a quick wash when you feel like they need it. The everyday wear is actually what keeps stainless steel looking its best.

The whole point of choosing quality materials is so you don't have to stress about maintenance. Your Goddess Shoulder Chain, your necklaces, your belly chains — they're designed to handle life. A little soap and water keeps them looking like the day you got them. That's it.

title: The Truth About Tarnish-Resistant Jewelry
excerpt: Tarnish-resistant doesn't mean tarnish-proof. Here's what you actually need to know.
content: Let's be honest: "tarnish-resistant" is one of those phrases that sounds like a promise but isn't quite one. It doesn't mean your jewelry will never tarnish. What it means is that it will take longer to tarnish, and when it does, it won't happen as dramatically. For everyday wear, that's actually the difference between a piece lasting you years and needing replacement every few months.

Most body jewelry marketed as tarnish-resistant is made from stainless steel—usually stainless steel, which is what we use for every piece we make here in our studio. The "stainless steel" matters. It's a specific alloy that includes chromium and nickel, which create a protective oxide layer on the surface. That layer is what slows down the tarnishing process. Silver and gold-plated pieces? They tarnish faster because there's no such protection built into the base metal.

Here's where people get confused: that protective layer isn't invisible or permanent. It can get compromised by prolonged exposure to salt water, chlorine, sweat, and certain chemicals. If you're wearing your jewelry every single day—which is kind of the point of body jewelry—you're testing that layer constantly. The water from the shower, the salt from your skin, the ocean on vacation. stainless steel handles it all better than most materials, but "better" isn't the same as "never".

The real advantage of tarnish-resistant jewelry is durability and low maintenance. You don't need special polishing cloths or cleaning routines. A quick rinse with soap and water, maybe a gentle wipe with a soft cloth, and you're done. Try that with silver and it'll oxidize faster. Try it with cheaper stainless steel and it might not hold up. With stainless steel, you can wear a piece like our Birthstone Gemstone Anklet every single day for years and it stays looking fresh.

One thing that surprises people: tarnish-resistant doesn't mean "never needs cleaning." It means the cleaning process is easy and infrequent. A light discoloration or slight dulling is normal over time, especially if you're wearing your piece constantly. But unlike sterling silver, it won't turn dark or require aggressive scrubbing to look good again. A rinse and you're back in business.

The durability matters most if you're looking for pieces that work with your actual life. You're not taking off your body jewelry before the gym, before bed, or before swimming. You want something that handles chlorine, sweat, and saltwater without demanding special care. That's where stainless steel shines. Our Pearl Body Harness is designed to be worn constantly, and the material is chosen precisely for that reason.

If you're comparing tarnish-resistant to gold-plated or silver-plated jewelry, here's the real talk: plating looks gorgeous at first, but it wears away. Once it does, you're left with the base metal underneath, which often discolors or deteriorates. Tarnish-resistant stainless steel doesn't have that problem. There's no layer to wear through. What you see is what you get, year after year.

The bottom line is this: tarnish-resistant jewelry is worth the choice because it's built for real life. You're not babying it. You're wearing it. title: Why Stainless Steel Jewelry Outlasts Gold Plated
excerpt: Gold plated fades. Stainless steel doesn't. Here's what actually happens to your jewelry.
content: Gold plated jewelry looks stunning at first. That's the whole point. But here's what happens next: you wear it, you shower in it, maybe you swim. The gold layer starts to chip away. Within months, you're seeing the base metal underneath. You didn't do anything wrong. That's just how gold plating works.

The problem is thickness. Gold plating is literally a microscopic layer of gold bonded to cheaper metal beneath. We're talking microns. It looks perfect when it's new, but daily wear tears through it fast. Water, sweat, soap, friction — these things don't care how expensive the piece was. They're going to wear that coating down.

Stainless steel is different. It's not a coating. It's the whole thing. stainless steel — the material we use for every piece — is waterproof and genuinely tarnish-resistant. You can wear it every single day without worrying about it degrading. Shower, swim, sweat, sleep in it. The metal stays the same.

Here's what matters: longevity. When you buy gold plated jewelry, you're buying something with an expiration date built in. You'll need to replace it. With stainless steel, you're buying something that's actually built to last. That's not marketing. That's just practical.

Cost matters too. Yes, stainless steel pieces cost less upfront than solid gold. But when you factor in replacement cycles, you're actually spending less over time. One Butterfly Charm Belly Chain in stainless steel will outlast multiple gold plated alternatives. That's real value.

The aesthetic is different, and that's okay. Stainless steel has a clean, modern shine that doesn't try to be something it's not. If you want that warm gold tone, sure, go for it. But understand what you're getting. You're getting a few months of shine, not years of wear.

We chose stainless steel for Bodystrands because we wanted pieces that actually work with your life. You wear body jewelry close to your skin, in water, while moving. It needs to survive that. When you pick up something like our Boho Belly Chain or Birthstone Bikini Clip Chain, you're getting something El and Gio handmade that'll still look good in a year, two years, five years.

The real question isn't stainless steel versus gold plated. It's what you actually want from your jewelry. Do you want something that looks perfect for a moment? Or something that stays beautiful because it's built to last? We know which one we'd choose.

The key is choosing one that matches the formality of your outfit. A delicate chain works for something simple and everyday. A bolder piece elevates a night out without trying too hard.

Think about the neckline of your dress too. If your backless dress has a high front, a shorter back chain keeps things balanced. If the front dips low, you can go longer in the back. It's about proportion, and your body is the canvas here.

Layering chains works if you're feeling it. A thinner back chain paired with a body chain or belly chain underneath creates depth. But don't overcomplicate it. Sometimes one piece says everything you need it to say. You'll feel the difference between wearing too much and wearing just right.

Material matters when something sits directly on your skin. Stainless steel doesn't tarnish, doesn't irritate, and doesn't break after one wear. You want something that moves with you and lasts through the entire night — and beyond. A good chain becomes part of your wardrobe, not something you worry about.

Color coordination is simpler than you think. If your dress is a dark color, warm metals like gold tones stand out beautifully. Silver works on everything, especially if your dress is metallic or neutral. The chain doesn't have to match your other accessories. It's its own statement.

Consider your hairstyle when planning your look. An updo or slicked-back hair gives the back chain room to shine. Loose waves create a softer frame. If you're wearing your hair down, a shorter chain keeps things from getting tangled. It's a small detail that makes a big difference in how the whole thing looks.

The best part about styling a backless dress with a body chain? You've made something beautiful even more interesting. You're not following a rule — you're trusting your instinct. And that confidence is what actually makes an outfit work.

title: Waterproof Jewelry: What It Actually Means (And What to Watch Out For)
excerpt: Not all 'waterproof' jewelry is created equal. Here's what the label actually means, what to avoid, and how to make your pieces last.
content: Waterproof jewelry is one of those terms that gets thrown around a lot. But there's a real difference between jewelry that survives a splash and jewelry you can actually wear in the ocean every single day.

True waterproof jewelry is made from solid stainless steel, not a coating. It doesn't plate, it doesn't coat, and it doesn't tarnish because there's nothing to tarnish. The metal itself is the finish.

Gold-plated and gold-filled pieces are different. They have a layer of gold over a base metal. Water doesn't instantly ruin them, but over time — especially with chlorine, saltwater, and sweat — that layer wears thin and the base metal shows through.
So when you see 'waterproof' on a product, the first question is always: what's it made of? Solid stainless steel? You're fine. Plated? You'll want to be more careful.

At Bodystrands, everything we make is stainless steel. We swim in our pieces, wear them to the beach, forget to take them off in the shower. That's the point — jewelry that lives your life with you. The Snake Belly Chain and the Cowrie Shell Anklet are two pieces people reach for exactly because of this.

The one thing even stainless steel doesn't love: harsh chemicals. Bleach, cleaning products, strong perfume directly on the metal. Spray your perfume first, let it dry, then put your jewelry on. That simple.

Storage matters too. Even waterproof jewelry benefits from being stored in a dry, airtight place when you're not wearing it. It keeps it looking new longer — not because it will tarnish, but because it prevents surface dust and micro-scratches.
The bottom line: if you want jewelry you don't have to think about, go solid stainless steel. It's not a compromise — it's actually the upgrade.
